children: agreed to pay New York City delivery drivers who were underpaid tips after the company moved tipping to after checkout in response to the city’s new minimum wage law.

removed the upfront tipping prompt, enabling customers to tip only after the order was delivered or assigned. New York City laws require food delivery services to offer customers an option to leave tips at checkout with a default option of 10% of the total cost of the order.

As a result of the change in its tipping choices, the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection found driver tips fell from more than $3 on average to less than $1. This amounted to more than $550M in lost tips to DoorDash
said in a social media post. “While these mistakes weren’t intentional, that doesn’t make them okay. We are sorry to the Dashers we let down.”

The company agreed to a $131.5M settlement, which includes $12.3M to delivery drivers who were underpaid or paid late, $83M to resolve a pay calculation dispute over on-call time for drivers, and $16.7M in civil fines paid directly to the New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection.
Of the $12.3M, every eligible driver will receive a minimum of $100, with the median settlement payment for affected drivers to be ~$48.

title: DoorDash to compensate NYC drivers who were undertipped
